summary: Each daily transaction's card number is looked up in the card cross-reference file. If the card isn't found, the transaction gets reason 100 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND', the account lookup is skipped and the transaction goes to the reject file instead of being posted.

then.text: The fail reason is set to 100.
The reason description is set to 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND'.
The account lookup and the account checks are skipped because the fail reason is no longer 0.
The transaction is not posted. The reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written.

title: Reject over-limit transaction based on current-cycle credit minus debit plus transaction amount
summary: For a found account, the program calculates current-cycle credit minus current-cycle debit plus the transaction amount. If the credit limit is less than the result, it sets reason 102 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION' and the transaction is rejected. The account's current balance is not used, and the result is held in a field with fewer integer digits than the account fields.

The credit limit, current-cycle credit and current-cycle debit are each signed amounts with 10 integer digits and 2 decimals.
The working balance holds only 9 integer digits and 2 decimals. Integer digits above the 9th are dropped when the result is stored (no ON SIZE ERROR is coded).

when.text: The working balance is calculated as current-cycle credit minus current-cycle debit plus the transaction amount.
The account credit limit is less than the working balance. If the limit is equal to or greater than the balance, this check passes.

then.text: The fail reason is set to 102.
The reason description is set to 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION'.
Because the fail reason is no longer 0, the transaction is not posted. The reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written.

summary: For a found account, the first 10 characters of the transaction's original timestamp are compared as text with the account expiration date. If the expiration date is earlier, the program sets reason 103 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION'. This check always runs after the over-limit check, so it replaces reason 102 when both fail.

The transaction is not posted. The reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written.

title: Route each daily transaction to posting or to the reject file, and set return code 4 when any are rejected
summary: Each daily transaction record is counted and validated, starting with reason code 0 and a blank description. If the reason code is still 0 afterwards, the transaction is posted. Otherwise the reject count goes up and a 430-byte reject record is written: the original 350-byte input record followed by an 80-byte trailer holding the 4-digit reason code and its 76-character description. At the end of the run the program sets return code 4 if at least one transaction was rejected.

given.text: Records are read one at a time from the daily transaction file until end of file. Each record that is read adds 1 to the processed-transaction count.
Before each transaction is validated, the failure reason code is set to 0 and the failure description is set to spaces, so nothing from the previous transaction carries over.
The validation trailer is 80 bytes: a 4-digit unsigned numeric reason code followed by a 76-character description.
A reject record is 430 bytes: 350 bytes of transaction data followed by an 80-byte validation trailer.

when.text: After validation, the program checks whether the failure reason code is still 0.

then.text: If the reason code is 0, the transaction is posted.
If the reason code is not 0, the reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written. The transaction is not posted.
The reject record's transaction data is the complete input daily transaction record, copied unchanged.
The reject record's trailer is the current reason code and description from validation.
The reject record is written as one record to the daily rejects file.
If the account rewrite during posting fails because the record key is not found, reason code 109 and the description ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND are set.

Surprising behaviour: the main loop checks the reason code only before posting and never after it. A reason code set during posting (such as 109) therefore produces no reject record and does not increase the reject count.
At the end of the run, the program displays the processed-transaction count and the reject count.
If at least one transaction was rejected, the return code is set to 4. Otherwise the program does not change the return code.

title: Posting updates or creates the transaction category balance record
summary: Each validated daily transaction is added to a category balance record keyed by account ID, transaction type code and category code. If no record exists for that key, a new one is created with the transaction amount as its balance. If one exists, the amount is added to its balance and the record is rewritten.

given.text: The daily transaction passed validation (no failure reason was set), so it is posted.
The category balance key is the account ID from the card cross-reference, plus the transaction's type code and category code.
The category balance is a signed amount with 9 integer digits and 2 decimal places.

when.text: The program reads the category balance file by that key. If no record is found, it sets the create flag to Y; otherwise the flag stays N.

then.text: If the create flag is Y, a new record is built. Otherwise the existing record is updated.
Create case: the record is initialized so the balance starts at zero.
Create case: the account ID, type code and category code are copied into the new record's key fields.
Create case: the transaction amount, with its sign, is added to the zero balance and the new record is written to the category balance file.
Update case: the transaction amount, with its sign, is added to the existing balance and the record is rewritten in place.
Update case: the ADD to the balance has no ON SIZE ERROR clause. If the sum has more than 9 integer digits, the high-order digits are silently dropped.

title: Posting updates the account balances and writes the transaction record
summary: After the category balance update, the transaction amount is added to the account's current balance. It is also added to the cycle credit total if the amount is zero or more, or to the cycle debit total if it is negative. The account record is then rewritten. Next, a transaction record is written: it copies the daily transaction's fields and adds a processing timestamp. If the account rewrite fails, reason 109 is set, but the transaction is still written and is not counted as rejected.

given.text: The account record being updated is the one read during validation, using the account ID from the card cross-reference.
The account's current balance is a signed amount with 10 integer digits and 2 decimal places.
The cycle credit and cycle debit totals are signed amounts with 10 integer digits and 2 decimal places.
The steps always run in this order, with no condition between them: category balance update, account update, then the transaction write.

when.text: A validated transaction is posted, and its amount is checked to see whether it is zero or more, or negative.

then.text: The transaction amount, with its sign, is always added to the account's current balance.
If the amount is zero or positive, it is added to the cycle credit total. If it is negative, it is added as a negative value to the cycle debit total, so that total goes down.
The updated account record is rewritten to the account file.
If the rewrite finds no record, reason code 109 and the text ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND are set.

The reason code is only checked before posting, to decide between posting and rejecting. A code of 109 set during posting therefore does not add to the reject count and does not write a reject record.
Before the next daily transaction is validated, the reason code is reset to 0 and the reason text to spaces.

The transaction record copies these fields from the daily transaction: ID, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant ID, merchant name, merchant city, merchant ZIP, card number and original timestamp.
The transaction record's processing timestamp is set to the formatted timestamp built just before it is moved in.
The timestamp is built from the current system date and time.
The current date and time are split into year (4 characters) followed by month, day, hour, minute, second and fraction (2 characters each).

The 26-character timestamp is laid out as: year (4), separator, month (2), separator, day (2), separator, hour (2), separator, minute (2), separator, second (2), separator, fraction (2), then a 4-character tail.
The date and time parts are copied in, the tail is set to 0000, the three date separators are set to '-' and the three time separators to '.'. The result is YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.ff0000.
The completed transaction record is written as a new record to the transaction file.
The transaction file is an indexed file keyed on FD-TRANS-ID.
The key FD-TRANS-ID is the first 16 characters of the written transaction record.

title: The last account group is never written back at end of file
summary: The end-of-file branch that should update the last account (ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) can never run. The loop condition is tested before each pass, so the loop ends as soon as END-OF-FILE becomes 'Y'. The last account in the category balance file therefore never gets its interest added or its cycle credit and debit zeroed, but its interest transactions are still written.

given.text: END-OF-FILE starts as 'N'.

The main loop repeats until END-OF-FILE = 'Y', and the test is made before each pass. Inside the loop, the ELSE branch that performs the account update is taken only when END-OF-FILE is not 'N' at the top of a pass.
For each category balance record whose DIS-INT-RATE is not zero, 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST is performed inside the loop.
1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST adds the record's monthly interest into WS-TOTAL-INT and right away performs 1300-B-WRITE-TX to produce an interest transaction.
The interest transaction record is written to the transaction file at that point, before and separately from any account update.

when.text: Reading the category balance file returns status '10' (end of file), which sets APPL-RESULT to 16.
APPL-EOF (APPL-RESULT value 16) causes END-OF-FILE to be set to 'Y'.

then.text: In the same pass, the inner check END-OF-FILE = 'N' is now false, so no more processing is done in that pass.
The loop condition END-OF-FILE = 'Y' is tested before the next pass, so the loop ends without evaluating the outer IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' again.
So the outer IF's ELSE branch, which performs 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT, is never run.

As a result, the last account group's WS-TOTAL-INT is never added to ACCT-CURR-BAL, its cycle credit and debit are not zeroed, and its account record is not rewritten. If the file is empty, no account is updated at all.
